brief: Writes a list out as text: as Ring code, with every item a text, joined with a separator, or converted between numbers and texts and in case.
detail: It is the writing-out helper of stzList, which builds one over itself for its Stringify, ToListInAString and ToListInAStringInShortForm methods; build one with new stzListStringify when you only need a text form. It works on its own copy, so a stzList passed in is never changed. A verb (Stringify, StringifyLists, StringifyObjects, Singlify) converts the held list in place and returns nothing, its Q form returning the stringifier for chaining; the past-tense forms (Stringified, ListsStringified, ObjectsStringified, Singlified) and the others (Lowercased, Uppercased, NumbersToStrings, StringsToNumbers, Join, ToCode) return the result and leave the stringifier alone. A number with decimals is written with two of them: 2.5 reads 2.50. StringsToNumbers raises on a text that is not numeric, and Join turns a sublist into an empty text. An object is written as the name of its variable, which is @noname when it has none. Hebrew, Arabic and emoji items are texts like any other.
